To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) active depression at age26 is associated with the most serious psychosocial problems; (2) past depression during the transition years is also associated with significant problems; and (3) the most serious psychopathology and functional deficits are associated with comorbid anxiety and substance abuse.

(1) active and past major depressive disorder (MDD) in young adulthood is associated with a range of impairments in psychosocial, educational, and work functioning; (2) the impairments associated with active and past MDD are similar, with the exception of work functioning, where individuals with active MDD experience the most impairment; and (3) the impairments in functioning associated with MDD persist into early adulthood, even after the depressive episode resolves.

(1) active major depression is associated with serious impairments in functioning, (2) past major depression is also associated with serious deficits in functioning, and (3) the deficits associated with past depression are comparable to those associated with active depression.
